questions.q: What are the two main components of Mr Herriot's treatment plan for Tricki during his hospital stay?
questions.a: The two main components are a strict controlled diet (starting with only water, then small meals) and enforced physical activity (running and playing with other dogs). A wrong answer that mentions "medicine," "injections," or "special tonics" reveals the student has not grasped that Herriot deliberately uses NO medical intervention — the story's irony is that the "surgery" is non-medical.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why Herriot gives Tricki only water for the first two days instead of food immediately.
questions.a: Herriot withholds food to break Tricki's addiction to constant eating and to let his overloaded digestive system rest; the water keeps him hydrated while his body begins to use stored fat. A wrong answer like "to punish him" or "because there was no food" shows the student misses the physiological rationale and misreads Herriot as cruel rather than clinical.

questions.q: On the third day, Tricki licks the empty supper bowls of the other dogs. Apply your understanding of the treatment plan to explain why Herriot allows this behavior instead of stopping it.
questions.a: Herriot allows it because Tricki is showing natural hunger and interest in food for the first time — a sign his metabolism is restarting. Licking bowls is harmless, provides mental stimulation, and reinforces that food is earned, not given freely. A wrong answer that says "Herriot was careless" or "Tricki was stealing" fails to see this as a deliberate therapeutic milestone.

questions.q: Compare Tricki's physical description on arrival ("bloated sausage," "bloodshot eyes," "listless") with the description after one week ("hard muscles," "spring in his step," "chasing rats"). Analyze how the author uses contrasting imagery to show transformation without stating "he lost weight."
questions.a: The author replaces static, round, passive imagery (sausage, bloated, listless) with dynamic, lean, active imagery (hard muscles, spring, chasing). The contrast shifts from shape words to action words, proving transformation through vitality not just size. A wrong answer that only lists "he got thinner" misses the literary technique of imagery contrast and fails to analyze the writer's craft.

questions.q: Evaluate whether Herriot's method would work for every overweight pet. Justify your judgment using evidence from the text and real-world pet care knowledge.
questions.a: Herriot's method works for Tricki because his obesity stems solely from overfeeding and inactivity — no underlying medical condition. For pets with thyroid issues, heart disease, or orthopedic problems, sudden forced exercise could be dangerous. The text shows Tricki had "no disease" — only "greed." A wrong answer that says "yes, it always works" ignores medical nuance; one that says "no, it's cruel" ignores the text's explicit statement that Tricki had no illness.

questions.q: Write a 3-day diary entry from Tricki's perspective during his hospital stay, showing his physical sensations and changing mindset. Use sensory details from the text (cold water, hard floor, other dogs' energy) and show internal change.
questions.a: A strong entry moves from Day 1: "Hunger gnawed, legs shook on cold concrete, missed mistress's warm lap" to Day 2: "Water tasted sweet, watched others run, felt strange lightness" to Day 3: "Chased a rat! Muscles burned but good. Food smells sharper. I am not the same dog." A weak entry stays emotional ("I miss Mrs Pumphrey") without physical progression or sensory grounding in the text's details.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: This topic covers the middle section of "A Triumph of Surgery" where Tricki undergoes a structured regimen at Mr Herriot's veterinary surgery: a strict diet of water followed by small meals, and enforced physical activity with other dogs, leading to his rapid physical ______ from an obese, listless "bloated sausage" into a fit, energetic animal.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are a vet watching a dangerously ______ dog arrive at your clinic.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can trace Tricki's day-by-day physical and behavioral changes during his hospital stay, cite specific textual evidence for each stage, and explain how Herriot's method (diet + activity) functions as both plot device and thematic statement about responsible care.
